messages:
elaine: Hey team — we started a scheduled API key rotation for customer AcmeCorp at ~08:30 UTC and right after a bunch of their calls started failing with 403. They also reported a sudden spike in usage billing alerts (surge of retry attempts). Could someone help triage?

sam: On it. Can you paste one of the failing request IDs or a short curl? 403 usually == invalid API key or scope.

elaine: Here's a scrubbed header/log: 
```
POST /v1/generate 403 {"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"key revoked"} request_id=req_43b2d
Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-acme-OLD
```
They said they rotated keys via our customer portal and the new key shows as active in their account.

sam: Thanks. Two immediate possibilities: 1) rotation created new key but we revoked the old one too early and some downstream systems (webhooks, batch jobs) still used old key -> 403 + retries. 2) New key has narrower scopes/limits and some endpoints rejected.

jordan: Also check secret propagation — if they rely on our Vault-sync or KMS agent, are env vars updated in their infra? If the new key wasn't pushed to all pods, they'll have mixed traffic.

alex: I can query API gateway logs for the request_id. Elaine, can you confirm which region? ap-southeast-1?

elaine: Yes ap-southeast-1.

alex: Found req_43b2d. Upstream shows Authorization header sk-prod-acme-OLD and our auth service flagged it as revoked token. Time: 2025-03-12T08:31:05Z. But I also see a flurry of requests from the same account using sk-prod-acme-NEW immediately after with status 200. So mixed.

matt: Customer says their background worker cluster is on an autoscaled fleet that reads secrets from HashiVault via an init script. They ran a rolling restart but might not have drained older pods.

sam: That fits. Two actionable items: 1) Recommend temporary grace/replay window for rotation so old keys remain valid for X minutes while clients converge. 2) Provide steps to rollout safely. Jordan, is grace supported?

jordan: We don't have an automatic "overlap" policy in the portal — rotate creates a new key and by default old_key -> revoked unless customer selects "keep for 15m". Our rotations-bot should have prompted that. I'll check rotation audit.

rotations-bot: rotation_event: customer=AcmeCorp user=elaine action=rotate timestamp=2025-03-12T08:30:55Z new_key_id=ak_9f8b kept_old=false

sam: Ah — kept_old=false. So the portal revoked old key immediately. That will cause partial failures until clients pick up the new key.

elaine: The customer claims portal UI showed a toggle to keep old key for 10m. They might have missed it.

alex: What's the fastest mitigation? We can un-revoke the old key temporarily. Jordan, can security re-enable it?

jordan: Yes we can re-enable old key, but we should log a short-lived reactivation and notify compliance. Re-enabling will flatten retry storms though. Recommend re-enable for 20 minutes and ask customer to finish rollout + restart remaining pods.

matt: I'll message AcmeCorp: ask them to restart any background workers that may cache the key (crons, lambda-like functions, sidecars). Also ask for list of integrations (webhooks, third-party infra) that might not be in their deployment manifest.

elaine: Sent: "We're seeing partial 403s after rotation. We're going to temporarily re-enable the old key for 20m to allow you to finish rollout. Please rotate again with overlap afterwards and restart all workers + clear any local caches." They responded: thanks, will restart 2 clusters; one still has older job queue consumer.

alex: I re-enabled ak_old (log id audit_774). It was accepted at 2025-03-12T08:36:10Z. API gateway now accepts both keys. 403 rate dropping.

sam: Good. After we stabilize, we should propose a safer default UX: portal default keeps old_key for 10m and shows a checklist: "restart pods, clear cache, update webhooks". Also we should add warning when KMS/Vault sync agents haven't confirmed update.

jordan: Agreed. Action items: 
- Re-enable old key (done).
- Add audit entry w/justification (I'll attach requestor comments).
- Update portal default to keep_old=true for 10m (product ticket).
- Add a post-rotate verification webhook (optional) to call customer URL and confirm receipt.

sam: For our support runbook, add a troubleshooting section: 
1) Ask for request_id and Authorization header sample.
2) Check rotations-bot audit for kept_old flag.
3) Query gateway logs for mixed keys.
4) If necessary, re-enable old key and advise customer to restart services.

matt: Customer confirmed both clusters restarted; error rate is back to baseline. They asked for a CSV of timeline for their audit. Elaine, can you attach logs?

elaine: Uploaded timeline + scrubbed logs to the case. Also included which nodes reported the old secret (node IDs).

jordan: I'll create a compliance-friendly entry: reason=partial outage mitigation, duration=00:20:15, actor=security_team_reenable.

sam: Long lead work: add portal check that warns when customers use HashiVault auto-sync: "We detected HashiVault integration. Rotating will revoke old key immediately unless you enable overlap". Also consider a Vault agent health check that reports last sync timestamp back to portal.

deploy-bot: deploy status: portal-fe v2.11.3 -> canary started (includes default keep_old toggle change).

elaine: Closing loop with AcmeCorp now. They've accepted mitigation and will re-run a rotation with overlap flag next week when they schedule a maintenance window.

matt: Marking this as P2 since broad customer impact was limited to one account and mitigation was quick.

sam: I'll draft a short KB article for support: "Handling failed rotations — mixed 403s after rotation" with repro steps and runbook.

jordan: I'll follow up with engineering to discuss adding reversible revocation window in the backend and a post-rotate verification API.

elaine: Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

sam: Thanks — closing thread once KB and portal changes are tracked in tickets.
